# Phase 1B: Y-sprite writer and a screen-space road-edge sample — 2026-10-21

**Question / hypothesis:** is the image-changing `$E6E0–$E6EF` Y-sprite RAM slot generated by the arcade sprite-list writer, and can the same controlled replay yield a small, independently reproducible Stage 1 road-edge observation? **Baseline:** the [saved-state range intervention](2026-10-21-arcade-sprite-range-localization.md). **Acceptance:** trace the sub-CPU writer without changing the replay screenshots; inspect a short private disassembly; sample the same visible left roadside boundary across adjacent centered/left/right frames; retain uncertainty about internal track and camera fields. **Result — partial PASS, verified by execution in MAME:** sub-CPU X writes the slot through a bounded routine around `$00E0A4–$00E0F4`, with an end marker in the centered run and another entry in steered runs. A fixed-image-color boundary sample gives 11 adjacent screen-space observations at three scanlines. It is **not** a decoded track/camera trajectory.

## Environment and method

**Verified by execution:** starting commit `327315298e2755efa0c5cd20982abeae93443186` on `experiment/perspective-road`; macOS 26.6.2 x86_64; MAME 0.289 binary SHA-256 `16f53f49def05df5d3377274ac3e78eea28249c52ae7a1fe80d2b367a78d18b4`; owner-local 53-file ROM manifest SHA-256 `b8894130f0d4081fb193fe675acd45f7ded2e0f3572a0d23560e9ebb969c6f2f`. Final Lua source SHA-256 `85cce6ae4c315fa5054b52d80be556dbb6ea598b93806e6eb8e85795a07a8a13`; road-edge sampler SHA-256 `d967eaa150e671e86f287201bd8db0c27756397cbfd8c5542ba88e5549199ff2`. The same ignored callback-950 MAME save state from the prior report was used for center, left and right. There was no Sega CD disc image, compiler, second emulator or physical-hardware run. These are emulated image positions in pixels, not hardware timing or host-speed measurements.

**Documented only:** the [MAME 0.289 Y-Board driver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mamedev/mame/mame0289/src/mame/sega/segaybd.cpp) maps sub-CPU-X `$180000–$18FFFF` as the `ysprites` memory share and draws Y sprites into a 512×512 source bitmap before applying rotation. The [MAME sprite implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mamedev/mame/mame0289/src/mame/sega/sega16sp.cpp) documents 16-byte entries, a high-bit end marker in the first word, linked entry indices and color-indirection tables. [MAME's Lua memory API](https://docs.mamedev.org/luascript/ref-mem.html) exposes the mapped address space and memory share; its [debugger API](https://docs.mamedev.org/luascript/ref-debugger.html) exposes write watchpoints. No upstream MAME code was modified.

**Verified by execution:** a private Lua probe read the `:ysprites` share as a 65,536-byte, big-endian, 16-bit share. Six selected offsets gave matching byte and word values through the share and sub-CPU-X program space at callback 966. The watchpoint replay used `PDRIFT_DEBUG_WATCH=ysprite`, which arms one 16-byte sub-CPU-X write watchpoint at `$18E6E0–$18E6EF` from callback 960 through 967 and focuses that CPU in the debugger. `PDRIFT_DISASM_DIR=.` optionally saves a short private disassembly around the writer. The command below runs inside each fresh ignored capture directory; omit `PDRIFT_STEER_PULSE` for center or set it to `64` for left:

```sh
PDRIFT_RAM_DIR=. PDRIFT_ROTATE_DIR=. PDRIFT_SWAP_DIR=. PDRIFT_SOURCE_DIR=. PDRIFT_SNAPSHOT_DIR=. PDRIFT_RAM_PROFILE=early PDRIFT_STATE_LOAD=/absolute/private/callback950.sta PDRIFT_STEER_PULSE=64 PDRIFT_DEBUG_WATCH=ysprite PDRIFT_DISASM_DIR=. /usr/local/Cellar/mame/0.289/bin/mame pdrift -rompath /absolute/private/rompath -noreadconfig -video none -sound none -nothrottle -seconds_to_run 18 -debug -debugger none -debuglog -autoboot_script /Users/murilo/repos/PowerDriftCD/tools/phase1b_mame_input.lua > phase1b-input.log 2>&1
```

Private evidence directories are `build/private/phase1b-ysprite-{probe,watch-center,watch-left,disasm-left}/`. Center and left watchpoint runs reproduced **all 11** corresponding callback-960–970 screenshots byte-for-byte against the untraced saved-state runs; the bounded disassembly run reproduced the left callback-967 screenshot. The private debug-log SHA-256 values are center `7dc4b364dafecdbe776ee05d4e654d56a5c490a9b4a14c959027eb9710445014` and left `cdec41168ae596302a9112bf309fcae2a102ea2e38bc504d7f8b61b4b9234855`. The private disassembly SHA-256 is `26aac4973be864fb4f6fa9dcf984200794c00c672c20b26a1e4c3eb4af593f0a`, and its replay input log SHA-256 is `c0d0a3005931306523ef70c8c5afa74e6ac3dc925cea04f5aa9f9c513b61d606`. Raw debugger output and disassembly remain ignored.

## Y-sprite slot result

**Verified by execution:** the centered trace has seven word writes within `$18E6E0–$18E6EC`, followed by a `$FFFF` first-word write marking the list end. The left trace has those same seven writes followed by another seven-word entry at the same slot. At callback 966, the centered first word is `$FFFF`; left and right are `$0006`. The last word remains `$E6F` in all three snapshots. Watchpoint PCs cluster around `$00E0A8–$00E0F4`. A bounded private disassembly shows the writer building entries through address registers `A2` and `A5`, with `A5` set 8 KiB beyond `A2`, and writing matching parameter groups into the two destinations. This explains the 8 KiB-separated differences observed in the prior report. The watchpoint PC is a debugger stop location and may be after the exact writing instruction; the disassembly, rather than a PC label alone, supports the writer interpretation.

**Verified by execution:** replacing only this 16-byte steered slot with the centered bytes in the earlier intervention changed 302 pixels at callback 967, within `x=103–210, y=149–160`. It did **not** move the left boundary sample at scanlines 162, 165 or 168 in that frame. The `$E400–$E7FF` intervention did move that sample by three pixels at scanlines 162 and 165. **Hypothesis:** `$E6E0` is an extra transient Y-sprite entry, plausibly a moving object or scenery element rather than the left edge itself. The test does not identify the sprite's graphic, palette, gameplay role, or precise renderer read instant. Calling it a track-data or camera field is **unsupported**. The CPU write watchpoint cannot see MAME's direct C++ reads from the sprite memory share.

## Reproducible screen-space boundary

**Verified by execution:** `tools/phase1b_road_edge_sample.py` samples screenshots 960–970 at rows `y=162, 165, 168`. At all 99 sampled rows, the first 16 pixels are the same sand-colored RGB `(214,214,132)`. The tool records the first x-coordinate, starting at 16 and below 128, with four consecutive pixels of another color. Visual inspection of the private screenshots places this transition at the left sand/curb/roadside boundary. It is a **screen-space color boundary**, not an extracted track edge coordinate, geometric curve or camera register. The script rejects images where the starting sand or sustained transition is absent rather than inventing a coordinate.

The `y=165` sample, in output pixels, is:

| 960 | 61 | 61 | 61 |
| 961 | 49 | 49 | 49 |

| 966 | 57 | 45 | 72 |
| 967 | 60 | 61 | 58 |

| 970 | 56 | 69 | 46 |

**Verified by execution:** before the steering response the three runs share the same coordinate; they then diverge, and the response is not monotonic. The sampler also records rows 162 and 168 and SHA-256 for every screenshot. Run it as follows:

```sh
python3 tools/phase1b_road_edge_sample.py build/private/phase1b-range-state-center build/private/phase1b-range-state-left build/private/phase1b-range-state-right > build/private/phase1b-road-edge-stage1.csv
```

The private 99-row CSV SHA-256 is `3e3b2aa0394ec34afcfd9d42a30dd19a1af85f83931d363aa473718a3f0695d0`. A second CSV from the traced center/left runs matched their 66 sampled values and screenshot hashes exactly; its SHA-256 is `44b718c18c20c351317b8d01acec85916caa69590564a6dd4d4d648476ff580c`. Sampling `y=165` alone cannot distinguish camera rotation from changed sprite geometry or occlusion. The red/white curb alternates under the selected row, so the boundary jumps even without steering; these numbers must not be interpreted as a smooth physical road trajectory.

**Next bounded test — hypothesis:** identify a source-space road/curb boundary in MAME's 512×512 Y-sprite bitmap at the same render instant, using a small isolated instrumented MAME build only if the current Lua interface cannot expose it. Compare that boundary with the saved rotation parameters and the final screen-space samples. This would separate sprite-source motion from whole-image affine motion before attempting an arcade-to-Sega-CD camera adapter. Preserve the existing Sega CD renderer and keep any extracted bitmap private. A complete real track/camera sequence and five-word interface compatibility remain **unsupported**.
